About us

Sport New Zealand promotes, encourages and supports sport and physical recreation to enrich the lives of New Zealanders. We passionately believe in the benefits and power of sport – for the enjoyment it brings, the satisfaction of achievement, and the pride we feel as a nation when our athletes succeed. We work with a range of organisations and people who share this passion, to create a world-class sports system at all levels – from grass roots to high performance - which will encourage more Kiwis to participate, and reap the benefits of a life-long involvement in sport. We aim to foster an informed and engaged online community, where everyone can be part of constructive conversation about sport and recreation in New Zealand. We welcome questions and commentary, including constructive feedback and differing opinions, however please ensure your comments are relevant and respectful. Differences of opinion are okay; personal attacks are not. To ensure that our social media platforms are used appropriately, we ask that people follow our community guidelines: https://sportnz.org.nz/resources/sport-nz-group-social-media-community-guidelines/ If you find content on one of our official pages which you believe breaches these guidelines please let us know by emailing sportnzcomms@sportnz.org.nz

    New guidance to make indoor sport, recreation and aquatics facilities more accessible is now available. Developed by Recreation Aotearoa with Sport New Zealand Ihi Aotearoa and BarrierFree, the guidance offers practical ways to improve accessibility – from early planning and design through to day-to-day operations. It is designed to help reduce barriers, so more disabled people and people with different access needs can take part in sport and recreation activities. Whether you’re planning, designing, managing or upgrading a facility, this is a great place to start. https://lnkd.in/enAJMTkP Image: A large, diverse group of people pose together in an indoor CrossFit gym against a bright red wall. This image is also featured on the cover of the guidance resource. A heading on the image reads 'Creating accessible and welcoming places and spaces, Guidance for indoor sport, recreation and aquatics facilities'.     What a moment for sport in Aotearoa! On Saturday we welcomed Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Prime Minister Christopher Luxon to celebrate 100 years of sporting connection between India and New Zealand. A century on from the Indian Army hockey team's first tour of New Zealand in 1926, Sport NZ and India's Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports signed the India-New Zealand Joint Action Plan on sport, building on the Memorandum of Cooperation signed last year. We had the chance to showcase New Zealand’s high performance system and innovation – a snapshot of what helps our athletes succeed on the world stage. We're also pleased to see support confirmed through the Event Boost Fund for 100 Years of Unity through Sport – a year-long programme of sport, community and cultural events across Aotearoa. A series of sporting events will take place later this year in Auckland, Christchurch, Hamilton, Tauranga and Wellington, with cricket, bowls and football matches already confirmed and more events to be announced. Sport has always been one of the strongest links between our nations and Saturday was a reminder of what we can achieve together through that connection. 🔗 Find out more and follow the programme: https://lnkd.in/eG2_26YC Photos: Mark Tantrum Photography New Zealand Cricket, Bowls New Zealand, New Zealand Football #100YearsOfUnityThroughSport

    ✨ Matariki Herenga Waka – Matariki, the gathering of people ✨ As the stars of Matariki rise, we pause to reflect on those who came before us, celebrate the people and communities around us today and look ahead with hope and purpose for the future. Sport and recreation have a unique way of bringing people together. Whether on the field, on the water, in the gym, in our parks and playgrounds or supporting from the sidelines, these shared experiences strengthen our connections to one another and to the places we call home. This Matariki, we acknowledge and thank the many volunteers, coaches, officials, leaders, athletes and organisations who help create a more active, healthy and connected Aotearoa New Zealand. We hope you find time to reconnect with whānau and community, reflect on what matters most and set intentions for the year ahead. ⭐ Mānawatia a Matariki ⭐ #Matariki #SportNZ #Aotearoa

    New Active NZ snapshots provide important insights into how neurodivergent young people and young new migrants are active in Aotearoa New Zealand. The findings reinforce that participation rates alone do not tell the full story. While some groups may appear to participate at similar levels, their experiences, barriers and levels of support can be very different. Key insights include: 🔸 Neurodivergent young people are more likely to be inactive and report more barriers to participation. 🔸Young new migrants are less active overall and spend less time being active each week. 🔸Both groups are less likely to participate in organised sport and club settings. Fun, and social connection remain strong motivators across all young people. These insights point to a clear opportunity to continue building a more inclusive, flexible and responsive system - one that better reflects the needs, preferences and experiences of a changing population. 👉️ Learn more here: https://lnkd.in/e7mNucDS
